clue.text: Disseminated sound of organ or flutes, but not drums?

definitions.text: Disseminated sound of organ or flutes, but not drums?

parts.words: Disseminated sound of organ or flutes, but not drums?
parts.note: background music relayed through speakers in shops; the joke is that organs and flutes really are pipe instruments while drums are not

explanation.surface: A question about which instruments can be heard broadcast around a building.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes you think of real instruments; the answer is the recorded background music fed through a building, punning on organ pipes and flutes.
explanation.definitionFit: Recorded background music relayed through loudspeakers in shops and lifts is the sense, an idiom for broadcast ambient sound.

clue.text: Habitat of arctic wolves, for example?

definitions.text: Habitat of arctic wolves, for example?

parts.words: Habitat of arctic wolves, for example?
parts.note: wolves hunt in groups, so a polar group of wolves suggests frozen floating sea masses, read as frozen groups

explanation.surface: A natural-history question about where wolves in the far north live.
explanation.walkthrough: Wolves run in packs, and in the arctic those could be 'ice packs': the frozen floes become a pun on wolf groups.
explanation.definitionFit: Floating masses of frozen sea are where polar animals roam, and wolves travel in groups, giving a double-meaning description.

clue.text: Quarter to five. Then a girl appears

parts.note: a quarter is a compass point, here East, abbreviated E
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Someone notes the time, a quarter to five, when a young woman turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarter to five' reads as a time, but it is E (a compass quarter) placed before V (five).
explanation.definitionFit: Eva is a female first name, so it stands as an example of a girl.

clue.text: Bomb factories?

explanation.surface: A dark question about places where explosives are made.
explanation.walkthrough: A Mills bomb is a British hand grenade of both world wars; separately, mills are works or plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mills bomb is a classic hand grenade, and mills are industrial works such as cotton or steel plants.

clue.text: Losing pace, but with hard work, out to succeed

indicators.note: the word for hard work sits outside, wrapped round the word for succeed

parts.note: a slog is a long stretch of tiring work
to win is to succeed

explanation.surface: A runner is flagging, yet working hard and determined to finish well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is read as 'outside', the container signal; the surface makes it sound like setting out to win.
explanation.definitionFit: Decelerating is the meaning: a runner who drops speed is getting slower.

clue.text: Basis of a mould that sounds like blue bloom?

indicators.note: tells you the entry is pronounced like the name of the blue plant

parts.note: the bright blue meadow plant often called bachelor's button

explanation.surface: A cook asks what thickens a set pudding, punning on a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: A mould here is a set dessert such as blancmange, thickened with maize starch; 'bloom' is a flower, not fungus.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine maize starch thickens and sets moulded desserts like blancmange, so it forms the base of such a pudding.

clue.text: The right weather?

parts.note: plays on the idiom 'right as ...', so the weather in that saying is the one that is right

explanation.surface: Someone asks what the correct kind of weather would be.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'as right as rain' means perfectly well, so the weather named in it is 'the right weather'.
explanation.definitionFit: Showers are the weather named in the idiom meaning perfectly fine, hence the weather that is right.

clue.text: Two materials destined reportedly for substitution

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric and lace an openwork fabric
rep is a ribbed fabric and lace an openwork fabric

indicators.note: signals that the word for destined is used for its pronunciation only

parts.note: destined means fated, intended

explanation.surface: Two fabrics fated to swap places with each other.
explanation.walkthrough: REP and LACE are both fabrics; 'reportedly' turns MEANT (destined) into the sound MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A swap of one thing for another is the sense shared by both nouns.

clue.text: Figures shown half-rising, holding silver

indicators.note: the turned word for half contains the symbol for silver
in a down clue the word for half is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: semi- is the prefix meaning half
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Statistics are displayed only partly improving, with silver among them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses the half word upwards in this down clue, making IMES; 'holding' wraps it round silver. 'shown' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pictures and likenesses are images, as are statues or shapes called figures.

clue.text: Rages about oil spill in harem

indicators.note: a spill scatters the letters of the two words before it into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is furious about an oil spill at a harem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' also suggests movement of letters; 'spill' rearranges RAGES and OIL together.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraglio is the women's quarters of a Muslim palace, a synonym for the household of wives.

clue.text: Traveller to have a meal, then see old movie

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative, a commercial traveller
to eat is to have a meal

explanation.surface: A salesman eats dinner and then watches a classic film.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'traveller' in British usage can be a travelling salesman, a rep.
explanation.definitionFit: A film shown again on television is a rerun, something seen before.

clue.text: Deformed arch is pointer to injury here?

indicators.note: something deformed is bent out of shape, so the letters of arch are reshaped

explanation.surface: A misshapen arch of the foot is a sign of where the hurt lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deformed' rearranges only the four letters of the arch word, making RACH. The definition is playful: the spine is where you might point when your back is injured.
explanation.definitionFit: The rachis is the spinal column, the place one indicates when complaining of a bad back.

clue.text: Morphia they use — it's making the blood run cold!

definitions.text: it's making the blood run cold!

indicators.note: the letters are used, reworked into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Patients given an opiate end up chilled to the bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'use' is the signal to rework MORPHIA and THEY together.
explanation.definitionFit: A dangerous drop in body temperature leaves circulation chilled, a medical condition of extreme cold.

clue.text: Blown up? Detail National Front involvement!

indicators.note: involvement suggests things twisted together, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: NF stands for the National Front, a British far-right party

explanation.surface: A report gives details of a far-right party's role in something.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Front is a British far-right party; 'involvement' mixes NF with DETAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something filled with air or exaggerated is puffed up, a synonym.

clue.text: Skier popping out to get equipment used when jumping

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A skier pops out to buy gear for jumping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'popping out' looks like a phrase, but only 'out' is the signal: SKIER and POPPING are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A cord swung over the head that children hop over is used in that playground exercise.

clue.text: A very cold draught

parts.note: draught reads as a chilly breeze, but means a drink taken, here one chilled

explanation.surface: A complaint about a freezing breeze through the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draught' looks like a current of air; it is a swallow of liquid, chilled with ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A chilled beverage served with ice is literally a cold swallow of liquid.

clue.text: At home, benefit books provided for those not willing to work

parts.note: in means at home
the dole is British slang for unemployment benefit
NT is the New Testament, the later books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A remark that staying home on benefits is for the workshy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the dole' is British slang for unemployment benefit; 'books' gives NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lazy, idle people avoid effort, which is what being averse to work means.

clue.text: Employment for lime production, perhaps, or getting rid of ashes?

definitions.text: Employment for lime production, perhaps, or getting rid of ashes?

parts.words: Employment for lime production, perhaps, or getting rid of ashes?
parts.note: lime and ash read as industrial materials, but they are trees, which these workers tend or fell

explanation.surface: A job in lime-burning or clearing away ashes from a fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lime' and 'ashes' suggest quicklime and fire residue; they are trees, cared for or felled by arborists.
explanation.definitionFit: Arborists are employed to grow, prune or remove trees such as limes and ashes.

clue.text: He must take staircase — no lift!

parts.note: a flight of stairs is a set of steps

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting the word no turns it upwards, so backwards

explanation.surface: A man must use the stairs because the elevator is out of order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lift' looks like an elevator but turns NO upwards to ON in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A wife's or husband's male child from an earlier marriage is a male relative, so 'He' covers him.

clue.text: He likes a flat green hat

explanation.surface: A man is fond of a flat green hat.
explanation.walkthrough: A flat green is the lawn for the game of bowls, so a bowls player likes it; a bowler is also a hard round hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of lawn bowls enjoys the flat green, and the hard felt derby hat shares the name.

clue.text: Leo in bed? This could be the prognosis!

definitions.text: Leo in bed? This could be the prognosis!

indicators.note: says the words before it could become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor's diagnosis for a lion lying about in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges LEO IN BED, and the whole clue describes the result: someone lazing in bed is plain lazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Utterly lazy is the idiom's sense: someone idle to the core lies about in bed.

clue.text: Worthless, they say, yet not thrown out

parts.note: yet as a conjunction means but

indicators.note: the letters of the word not are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Something said to be worthless has nevertheless been kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they say' marks the idiom 'not worth a button'. 'thrown out' rearranges NOT into TON.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'not worth a button' makes the small fastener a byword for something of trifling value.

clue.text: On turning up, is put in taxi — that's fundamental!

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reads the whole assembly from bottom to top
the word is goes inside the word for taxi

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: A passenger climbs into a taxi, which is presented as essential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' makes CISAB, and 'On turning up' reverses the whole thing, upwards in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Essential and elementary are synonyms of a fundamental, rudimentary thing.

clue.text: Students of the past

parts.note: reads like historians, but means former pupils of a school or college

explanation.surface: People who study history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Students of the past' suggests historians; it means former students.
explanation.definitionFit: Graduates or former pupils of an institution are its past students.

clue.text: The old sighed, on being taken to court — holding tears back

indicators.note: the word for taken to court contains the other piece

parts.note: to be sued is to be taken to court

indicators.note: the word for tears is read backwards

parts.note: rips are tears

explanation.surface: An elderly person sighs on being prosecuted, fighting back tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old' marks the answer as an archaic word. 'back' turns the tears word into SPIR before 'holding' encloses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Breathed out heavily is the archaic verb's meaning, an old literary synonym.

clue.text: It is charged for portion, excluding wine

indicators.note: the word for wine is taken away from the word portion

parts.note: port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A diner is billed for a serving that does not include drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' suggests billing, but means electrically charged; 'excluding' removes PORT from PORTION.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom or molecule with an electric charge is the physics term.

clue.text: Top-class artist bowled over by song

indicators.note: being knocked over turns the pair of pieces back to front

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A great painter is overwhelmed by a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowled over' reverses AI RA as a whole to give AR IA.
explanation.definitionFit: An operatic solo melody is a vocal piece, a type of song.

clue.text: Royal sea commander

parts.note: reads as a naval admiral, but recalls the English king who ordered the tide to retreat

explanation.surface: A monarch who is also an admiral.
explanation.walkthrough: It suggests a naval officer; the legend is of the Danish-English king who commanded the tide not to come in.
explanation.definitionFit: The eleventh-century monarch legendarily ordered the waves back, so he gave commands to the ocean.
